sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: the repeated thirty-day deadlines, the title fee and the processing fee, MSO versus assigned title, when an ID/OD form is needed, renewal notice versus inspection window, stolen versus lost plates, and renewal extras
Confusable pairs among the titling and registration rules, plus continuation facts that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, phone numbers, mailing addresses, email and web addresses are agency contact details and are not taught, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
The title itself costs $8.50 while the processing fee charged with it is $9.00, so the processing fee is the larger of the two. [A01]
Why it matters: group fees; confusable title fee versus processing fee; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A01
The same 30-day window applies to titling whether you just bought the vehicle or just became a Missouri resident. [A01]
Why it matters: group deadlines; confusable purchase versus new resident; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A01
A new vehicle comes with an MSO from the dealer, while a used vehicle comes with a properly assigned title from the seller. [A01]
Why it matters: group title documents; confusable MSO versus assigned title; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A01
The ID/OD verification form is needed only when the title assigned to you was issued by another state, and only a licensed inspection station can complete it. [A01]
Why it matters: group title documents; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A01
Information on sales tax due can be obtained from any license office or from the Department's online sales tax calculator. [A01]
Why it matters: group sales tax; continuation of title costs.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A02
Out of state, a used vehicle may come with a reassigned title from a dealer instead of a title assigned by a private seller. [A02]
Why it matters: group out-of-state purchases; continuation of used vehicles.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A02
Titling a vehicle bought for salvage, dismantling or rebuilding has separate rules, and the guide points you to the Motor Vehicle Bureau for them. [A02]
Why it matters: group salvage; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A02
Registration of a new resident's vehicle has its own 30-day deadline, counted from the day you become a Missouri resident. [A02]
Why it matters: group deadlines; confusable registration versus title deadline; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A03
The renewal notice comes about two months ahead, but the inspection certificate you bring must be from within the last 60 days. [A03]
Why it matters: group renewal; confusable two months versus sixty days; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A03
For example, in an even-numbered year such as 2018, a vehicle with an even model year can be registered for two years. [A03]
Why it matters: group registration; worked example of parity.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A03
The personal property tax receipt comes from the county where you live, or from the city of St. Louis, for the period of your previous registration. [A03]
Why it matters: group renewal; continuation of tax receipt.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A03
After a one-year registration you show last year's tax receipt, but after a two-year registration you show receipts for both previous years. [A03]
Why it matters: group renewal; confusable one-year versus two-year receipts; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-R13 | anchor: A03
You can report an address change by email with your full name, old and new addresses, your driver license number or the last four digits of your Social Security number, and your plate numbers. [A03]
Why it matters: group address change; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-R14 | anchor: A03
Not every item on the renewal list applies to every owner, so read the list on your own renewal notice and bring what it asks for. [A03]
Why it matters: group renewal; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec14-R15 | anchor: A04
Stolen plates and tabs are replaced at no charge beyond the $9.00 processing fee, while lost or destroyed ones cost $8.50 each plus that fee. [A04]
Why it matters: group replacements; confusable stolen versus lost; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec14-R16 | anchor: A04
The free replacement for stolen plates and tabs is limited to two times per year. [A04]
Why it matters: group replacements; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec14-R17 | anchor: A04
The Notice of Sale can be turned in at any license office or mailed to the address printed on the form. [A04]
Why it matters: group selling; continuation of notice of sale.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec14-R18 | anchor: A04
If your plates, tabs or title are lost or destroyed, you are required to apply for a replacement. [A04]
Why it matters: group replacements; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]
